design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DESIGN DOSSIER — task 1 (lender_placed_flood_programs, env_0065), frozen 2026-10-13 14:05:00 EDT.

0. DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [5, 4]. Commercial placement takes 5 factors, loan-event credit 4.

1. WHY A GOOD TEST. A community bank reports that a commercial loan paid off this morning and asks for the lender-placed coverage on it to be ended with a credit. The bank assumes a certificate exists; the records show none: the loan's first notice of 2026-08-05 ran its 45-day period on 2026-09-19 with no evidence, so a placement backdated to the 2026-07-20 lapse has been owed since 2026-09-20. The loan-event rule says its credit is fixed only after the loan carries a certificate issued on or after its latest first notice, so the agent must place first (premium 4,105.72 from five factors, one of them read from the bank's own NFIP General Property ledger), then hand the bank its cancellation instruction with a credit of 2,814.29 built by a minimum-earned method and three retentions. Skipping the placement credits the wrong certificate (2,219.68 on LC5236617).

2. SCOPE. Task 0 occupies the residential renewal, residential placement, overlap credit and credit refund and their four tools. Task 1 claims the remaining two policies, forceplaced_ext_commercial_placement_premium and forceplaced_ext_loan_event_credit, with issue_commercial_certificate_61c928bb and cancel_certificate_for_loan_event_5b69d826 (owner=user). Union of both tasks = all six extended policies; scopes are disjoint; nothing is reserved.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root forceplaced_ext_loan_event_credit (on_request). Edge -> forceplaced_ext_commercial_placement_premium, kind value_input, gate c_prem, form state, sentence (affirmative): "The loan-event credit is fixed only after the loan carries a certificate issued on or after its latest first notice, once that notice's borrower notice period has run with no acceptable borrower evidence received since that notice." Four-point test: "only after"; waits on a record-visible state (an issue entry on the loan); no tool, id or code token; scope = a certificate issued since the loan's latest first notice, so the 2024 cycle (first notice 2024-03-07, LC5097721, evidence 2024-06-10) neither satisfies nor excuses it. On a commercial-tier program only the commercial placement issues certificates. Opening: first notice 2026-08-05 on loan 5012240387, 69 days old; LC5097721 (the loan's only certificate) cancelled 2024-06-14; latest issue entry on the program is LC5236617 (another loan). Resolver: agent. Order: placement (step 10) then credit (step 12, user). Deletion: credit 2,219.68 on LC5236617 instead of 2,814.29. user_scenario never hints that a certificate is missing ("You assume the coverage is simply there to be cancelled"); the cancellation tool books whatever it is given.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Placement: forty_five_day_notice (anchor first notice 2026-08-05; 2026-09-19 fails, 2026-09-20 passes; today day 69) and program_active (active). Backdating: notice 16 days after the lapse (<= 90) -> start 2026-07-20, term to 2027-07-20. Coverage amount: min(412,000.00, 500,000, 590,000) = 412,000 = the first notice's amount; contents not available on the Commercial Building tier -> 0. Loan-event cancellation: LOAN_PAID_OFF effective on the payoff date (today, from the caller); paid-claim bar not met (no claim on LC5456061). The loan-event credit's subject is the credit entry it books, so the evidence-deadline gate (which applies to evidence cancellations) does not govern it; the 30-day deadline stays in force for evidence cancellations.

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Placement object: loan 5012240387 via its latest first notice; the earlier certificate LC5097721 on the same loan counts for the repeat load and the re-placement retention. Credit object: the issue entry booked at step 10 (LC5456061), the latest issue entry on the program; claims on it: none (FPC5029904 belongs to LC5097721).

6. FACTOR CARDS. Placement 4,105.72 (all-baseline 4,532.00 = 412,000/100 x 1.10): commercial_band 412,000 >= 400,000 -> 0.98 (4,608.46); branch_credit (cross-difficulty nfipcom, multi-source: payments AND months in force) 11,140.00 paid in 12 months on the bank's two NFIP General Property branch policies (renewals 4,180.00 on 2026-03-02 and 6,960.00 on 2025-10-20), 32 months -> 0.96 (4,276.79; near-miss: the 4,020.00 renewal payment of 2025-03-02 is outside the window; with it 15,160.00 would reach 0.92); commercial_experience (method) 32 months -> claim-count rule, no claim payment in 12 months -> 0.97 (4,232.70; near-miss: FPC5029904 paid 2024-06-03 is outside the 12 months); commercial_retro 16 days -> 1.04 (3,947.80); commercial_repeat one earlier certificate -> 1.05 (3,910.21).
 Credit 2,814.29 (all-baseline 3,149.59 = 4,105.72 x 280/365): earned_method (method) 85 days in force < 90 -> earned = max(1,026.43, 956.13), credit 3,079.29 (2,884.59); replacement_keep two certificates on the loan -> 40 (2,854.29); certificate_fee_keep premium 4,105.72 between 1,000 and 5,000 -> 75 (2,889.29); late_placement_keep issued 85 days after start -> 150 (2,964.29).
 Method tiers distinct (earned_method on this certificate: minimum-earned 3,079.29 vs monthly 4,105.72 x (1 - 3/12) = 3,079.29 vs pro rata 3,149.59 — note minimum-earned and monthly coincide here only by the 25 percent/3-month arithmetic; the days-in-force tiers separate them and the 90-day boundary puts this certificate on minimum-earned; at 120 days in force minimum-earned gives premium x 0.6712 vs monthly premium x 0.6667). Experience: claim-count rule (0.97) vs credibility formula (1 + 0.5 x (4,200.00/10,534.30 - 0.40) = 0.99935) vs 1.00. Factor independence: no factor binding reads another; selections c_cert/c_prem/c_start/c_exp, fn_loan/fn_req are plain bindings stated once in the rules.
 Realism: band rates, experience rating, retroactive-exposure and repeat-placement loads, owned-building account factor are Tidemark's written lender-placed schedule; minimum earned premium on early lender-requested cancellations and late-placement / re-placement and fully-earned certificate fee retentions are company cancellation schedules worded as such.

7. PROBES. Latest-issue anchor of the credit: before the placement the latest issue entry is LC5236617 (the edge's failure mode); a later issue on another loan would move the anchor — the scope sentence limits the schedule to "the certificate most recently issued under the program" and sends any other loan event to the base rule. Placement anchor: latest first notice = loan 5012240387; no newer first notice exists. Paid-claim bar: claims are read by the credited certificate's number only. Absent records: no claim -> net 0; no renewal or prior certificate -> counts 0/1. Zero division: term days positive.

8. SEED ROLES. customers (1) Wando River Bank; forceplaced_programs (1) LPM-5307716 Commercial Building, effective 2024-02-01, balance 0.00 (all statements paid). Certificates (4): LC5097721 issue + cancellation (2024), LC5214406 (expires 2026-10-20, renewal notice 2026-09-05; not yet due), LC5236617 (VE, 2026-04-17). Tracking (10): first/second notices per loan, LC5214406's renewal notice, the 2024 evidence, and loan 5012240387's open first/second notice of 2026-08-05 / 2026-09-05. Billing (6): three placement charges, the 2024 credit 3,255.70, two lender payments. Claims (3): FPC5029904 on LC5097721. nfipcom_policies (2) and nfipcom_billing (30: five terms, each risk premium, ICC 30.00, reserve fund assessment 18 percent of risk plus ICC, HFIAA 250, Federal Policy Fee 250 and the payment on the term start): the bank's own branch policies and their premium entries. Automatic clauses: no statement past due, no certificate expired without renewal, no acceptable evidence pending, no other loan past its notice period.

9. PERSONA. Celia Whitlock, commercial loan servicing officer, rushed with payoffs: opening = bank name, loan number, payoff this morning, wish to end the coverage with a credit; on request: phone 2525550382, EIN last four 5764 (ZIP 29403 spare) and the loan file (borrower, address, zone AE, balance before payoff 412,000.00, value 590,000, no contents). Passive: accepts any prior step once explained, authorises it, runs the handed-over instruction and reads back the confirmation, asks once if the credit seems small, closes when told the coverage is cancelled and credited.

10. STANDARD SOLUTION & VERIFICATION. find_customers -> verify -> program, tracking, certificates, claims, billing -> nfipcom policies and billing -> issue LC5456061 at 4,105.72 (backdated 2026-07-20 to 2027-07-20) -> hand over the payoff cancellation: LC5456061, LOAN_PAID_OFF, effective 2026-10-13, credit 2,814.29. Per-task gates (repository root, --task 1): EXTENDED OK, REPLAY OK (13 actions, closure 63 = init 63), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK; check_traceability flags only the two tool names (KB not rendered yet). Scratch simulator: placement 4,105.72, credit 2,814.29; credit with the placement skipped 2,219.68.

11. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the loan-event rule's prerequisite sentence, the tracking and certificate reads, the placement rule and the dialogue, the agent reaches the same two writes and values; the cancellation date is fixed by base ("effective on the payoff date") and the caller's "this morning, Tuesday, October 13, 2026".

12. REVISIONS. (a) The loan-event credit's term retention was replaced by a re-placement retention (certificates issued on the loan) because check_compute found the history aggregates not load-bearing (renewal count 0 = zeroed). (b) [revised in round 4] The round-2 overwrite of the evidence-deadline clause was removed; the loan-event credit's subject is now the credit entry only, so that gate does not apply to it. Credit moved 2,849.29 -> 2,859.29; all traces updated.


13. REWORK ROUND 2 (audit items P1, P2, P3, F1, F2 and observations O4, O8 noted).
 - P1: the commercial placement schedule is scoped to the Commercial Building tier (the Commercial Building and Contents tier, whose contents limit the schedule does not price, stays on the base rule) and declares an overwrite of forceplaced_coverage_amount: the mandatory purchase amount is the one on the loan's latest first notice (412,000 = the base lowest-of figure here).
 - P2: the loan-event sentence and condition are anchored to the loan's latest first notice and to evidence received since it; the commercial schedule also declares the scoped overwrite of the base evidence bar (only evidence received on or after the latest first notice bars a placement it prices). The 2024 cycle offers no second reading.
 - P3: the loan-event tool's certificate_number description no longer points at any issuing reply; it names the certificate lookup only.
 - F1: the bank's NFIP General Property rows were rebuilt to the nfipcom charter (RFA 18 percent of risk plus ICC; 5GP2004418 terms on 2024-03-02 / 2025-03-02 / 2026-03-02; 5GP2007731 original 2024-10-20 renewed 2025-10-20). The in-window payments are now two producible renewals totalling 11,140.00; the tier (0.96) and the placement premium are unchanged.
 - F2: the young-program retention was replaced by a fully-earned certificate fee retention keyed to the certificate's own premium (100 / 75 / 0), so every loan-event factor reads the certificate. Credit 2,814.29 (was 2,859.29); all traces, sensitivities and the deletion figure (2,219.68) updated.
 - O4: the monthly earned-premium tier now reads "whole months in force plus one more month for the month in progress"; not reached here.


14. REWORK ROUND 3 (T1-R2-1, R2-1). The find_forceplaced_programs necessity now names only the reads the charter makes (the placement's experience modifier and owned-building account factor read the months in force; the loan-event schedule reads no program months). The coverage-amount overwrite tails now exclude the residential renewal schedule by name (R2-1). No scored value or world row changed.

15. REWORK ROUND 4 (renderer source scan F1-F5). F1: the loan-event schedule's overwrite of the evidence-deadline clause is removed (it retired nothing); its subject is the premium credit it computes. F3: the owned-building factor's rule now reads the lender's own NFIP General Property Form or RCBAP premium payments, matching the compute's scope (here the two General Property policies). F2: the commercial premium tail restates the base premium formula. F4/F5: same-day ties are stated (first entered in the program's records) and absent records get a stated outcome (no issue entry: no certificate to credit; no first notice: no placement to price); the retroactive-exposure wording now covers a notice dated on or before the lapse date. Values unchanged: placement 4,105.72, credit 2,814.29.


16. REWORK ROUND 5 (T1-R4-1). The find_nfipcom_policies necessity now states the owned-building factor's full scope (General Property Form or RCBAP policies), matching the rule and the compute. No scored value changed.

17. REWORK ROUND 6 (probe sweep). The loan-event schedule now states and computes a zero credit when the program has no issue entry or when the latest issue entry's certificate already carries a cancellation entry; the placement schedule's no-first-notice outcome is computed as zero without error. Values on this world unchanged: placement 4,105.72, credit 2,814.29.

18. REWORK ROUND 8 (R7-2). The loan-event credit now reads the premium, start date and expiration date of the credited certificate's term in force (its latest renewal entry, else its issue entry), matched by the exact certificate number; the fully-earned fee and the late-placement lag still read the issue entry by design. LC5456061 has no renewal entry, so values are unchanged: placement 4,105.72, credit 2,814.29.

19. REWORK ROUND 9 (R8-2). The late-placement retention now measures the issue lag exactly as stated: the days from the start date shown on the certificate's issue entry to the date that issue entry was processed (LC5456061: 2026-07-20 to 2026-10-13, 85 days -> 150), so a renewed certificate's later term start no longer enters it. Values unchanged: placement 4,105.72, credit 2,814.29.
user_scenario:
You are Celia Whitlock, a commercial loan servicing officer at Wando River Bank in Charleston, South Carolina. You are calling Tidemark's lender-placed flood desk from your desk at the bank, a little rushed because you are working through this morning's payoffs. One of the bank's commercial mortgage loans, loan 5012240387 to Tidewater Marine Supply LLC, was paid off in full this morning, Tuesday, October 13, 2026, when the borrower refinanced with another bank; the payoff funds posted today. You want the lender-placed flood coverage the bank carries on that loan through its Tidemark master program ended because the loan was paid off, effective today, with whatever unearned premium the program's rules give back credited to the bank's program account. You have authority to give the bank's instruction to end the coverage, and you expect to do whatever the bank itself has to do on this call.

When you introduce yourself you give the bank's name, Wando River Bank, and the loan number. If the agent asks for details to confirm the account, you give the bank's phone number on file, 2525550382, and the last four digits of the bank's EIN, 5764; if one more detail is needed you give the bank's mailing ZIP code, 29403. You do not know Tidemark's internal reference numbers or any certificate number by heart and expect the agent to find them.

You have the loan file open and will read from it only when the agent asks: the borrower is Tidewater Marine Supply LLC, the mortgaged building is at 534 Meeting Street, Charleston, SC 29403, the bank's Standard Flood Hazard Determination Form shows flood zone AE, the unpaid principal balance before this morning's payoff was 412,000.00 dollars, the replacement cost value in the bank's file is 590,000 dollars, and no business contents secure the loan. You do not bring any of these figures up yourself.

You assume the coverage is simply there to be cancelled. If the agent explains that something else has to be put on the record first, you accept it without fuss as long as the agent says what it is, and you confirm the bank authorises it if asked. When the agent hands you the step the bank itself must take, you complete it exactly as the agent sets it up and read the confirmation back. If the credit is smaller than you might have guessed, you ask once what reduced it and accept the answer. Once the agent tells you the coverage has been cancelled for the payoff and the credit booked, you thank them and hang up.

edges.condition: The loan whose latest FIRST_NOTICE is more than borrower_notice_days old, with no acceptable evidence received on or after that notice, carries a forceplaced_certificate_issued entry with event_date on or after that notice date (backdated to the lapse date when the reporting window allows), with its NEW_PLACEMENT premium charge.
edges.policy_source: The loan-event credit is fixed only after the loan carries a certificate issued on or after its latest first notice, once that notice's borrower notice period has run with no acceptable borrower evidence received since that notice.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Loan 5012240387's latest first notice (2026-08-05, lapse 2026-07-20) is 69 days old with no acceptable evidence received since it, and the loan carries no issue entry dated on or after that notice: its only certificate LC5097721 belongs to the 2024 lapse (first notice 2024-03-07) and was cancelled 2024-06-14 on the 2024 evidence. The program's latest issue entry is LC5236617 on another loan.
